A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WildAvatar, retaining the 10,647-clip dataset and identifiable pipeline and avatar experiments. Text, tables, figures and equations support reliable comparison. V4 includes Appendices A–D; the supplied v1 ends with references.

before.justification: V1 reports original dataset analyses, per-subject reconstruction experiments in Table 2, and generalization experiments with and without WildAvatar training in Table 3.

after.justification: V4 reports original annotation evaluations, filtering analyses, avatar experiments and qualitative comparisons, including evidence in its appendices.

M1.justification: The four-stage annotation backbone remains, but v4 adds multi-expert prediction fusion and agreement-based filtering across detection, pose and SMPL models. Protocol III also introduces PCK-based consistency filtering between projected SMPL joints and estimated 2D keypoints. These materially extend the procedure described with YOLO and PARE in v1.

E1.justification: V4 adds quantitative SMPL annotation evaluation on EMDB and consistency and qualitative comparisons using 3DPW, extending evaluation beyond avatar rendering and dataset characterization. WildAvatar and the four laboratory datasets remain in generalization experiments; ZJU-Mocap's separate per-subject comparison disappears.

E2.justification: V4 Table 2 adds eight annotation comparators: SPIN, VIBE, PARE, TRACE, CLIFF, TCMR, HybrIK and HMR2.0. Table 4 additionally compares HMR2.0 annotations against the proposed annotations for downstream reconstruction. The seven avatar reconstruction methods and four generalization methods are retained.

E3.justification: Per-subject evaluation changes from 10 subjects with 10 training and 10 test frames each to 133 subjects with 100 training and 100 test frames each. V4 adds an annotation-source control and new protocols using EMDB-1, joint/vertex errors, PCK at threshold 0.1 and SOIOU. Cross-version reconstruction scores therefore are not directly comparable.

E4.justification: V4 adds sequential filtering/refinement analysis measuring consistency and retained clip counts in Table 3. Appendix figures examine unusual viewpoints, high-SSIOU clothing examples, coarse versus refined SMPL, and accepted/rejected masks. V1's detailed per-subject failure-case comparison is replaced by annotation-source comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for experimental results. V4's standard deviation across annotating experts is a filtering component, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V4 adds EMDB and filtering results and replaces the per-subject results under its revised protocol. Corresponding generalization entries also change: the first MPS-NeRF row's laboratory novel-view PSNR changes from 18.46 to 16.99, while WildAvatar generalization scores remain unchanged. The resolution chart corrects the 720×1280 label from 70.3% to 23.1%, and Appendix D adds population and scene statistics.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies constant body shape across frames, temporal and alignment losses, GMM pose-prior regularization, and their weighted objective in Equations 1–4. V1 describes refinement verbally. This adds limited mathematical specification; neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 primarily claims a large in-the-wild dataset, challenging avatar benchmarks and improved generalization. V4 elevates the annotation/filtering pipeline to a central contribution and adds claims of superiority on EMDB and improved downstream reconstruction through better annotations. The dataset-scale and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of filtering benefits, improved extremity alignment and high SSIOU arising from loose clothing rather than erroneous fitting. It removes v1's detailed annotation-noise, clothing and lighting challenge discussion, explicit limitations concerning backgrounds, static activities and human interactions, and specific portrait-rights and bias caveats.

D1.justification: The appendices newly document model variants, filtering thresholds, frame selection, loss weights, L-BFGS settings, pipeline runtime and evaluation details. V4 also supplies a project address and S-Lab License 1.0 statement. V1's per-baseline training-time and rendering-FPS entries are removed.

R1.justification: V4 substantially strengthens positioning around automatic SMPL annotation and filtering, including direct comparison with HMR2.0. It adds relevant references such as EMDB, HMR2.0, TCMR, Detectron2, HRNet and DWPose, and extends application positioning to human interactions and relightable avatars. The earlier dataset and avatar-method survey largely remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the pipeline. Existing collection, processing and dataset-analysis material is reorganized into Methodology, WildAvatar and appendices, while the experimental narrative shifts from diagnosing reconstruction challenges to demonstrating annotation benefits.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column layout, redesigns the opening overview and dataset graphics, expands the pipeline diagram, and adds filtering illustrations and annotation tables. It replaces the per-subject comparison display and adds six appendix figures. Retained generalization illustrations are reformatted and faces are blurred.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens a central weakness of v1: annotation quality was asserted without direct quantitative validation. EMDB evaluation, staged filtering analysis and downstream annotation-source comparisons provide important supporting evidence, while the appendices make the pipeline substantially more reproducible. These gains outweigh the removal of useful failure and limitations discussion. A remaining documentation problem is the unexplained relationship between selecting 20 frames per clip and evaluating 200 frames per subject.
